title: A Vector for the Horizon
premise: When gravity stutters for nine seconds across the whole system, terraformer and freight pilot Bram Eastwick realizes the 'anomaly' was a handshake—a dead man's failsafe keyed to Bram's own biometrics, inherited from a parent they never knew. The signal is a ledger of crimes committed by the Meridian Combine, the corporation that quietly owns the contested orbits, and it will broadcast to every colony unless Bram delivers the decryption key to the edge-of-dead-space relay. Hunted by Combine enforcers and shadowed by their loyal crew, who each have reasons to want the truth buried, Bram must decide whether justice outside the law is worth burning the only family they have left. In the end Bram reaches the relay, chooses to broadcast the ledger at the cost of their ship and their anonymity, and survives—unrecognized, finally free, planting the first real garden for people who will know their own history.
about_author: R. M. Fairweather is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent a decade writing incident reports before turning to fiction. They live somewhere with unreliable weather and write about people who fix things no one thanks them for.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Bram Eastwick's POV aboard freighter Kestrel's Wake. Mid-haul through contested orbits, gravity fails for exactly nine seconds; Bram's implants log a data spike keyed to their own genome. Emotional beat: unease—the invisible life Bram built is cracking open.

chapters.title: The Garden for the Unborn
chapters.summary: Bram tends the orbital greenhouse they're contracted to maintain, seeds meant for colonists a century away. Crewmate Sefa notices Bram's distraction. Emotional beat: tenderness and denial; Bram wants to be a gardener, not whatever the spike says they are.

chapters.title: Inheritance in a Dead Man's Voice
chapters.summary: Bram decrypts a fragment: their estranged parent, long presumed dead, left a failsafe ledger of Meridian Combine crimes, triggered by blood. Emotional beat: grief and anger at a parent who weaponized absence into duty.

chapters.title: Crew of Small Complicities
chapters.summary: POV shifts to engineer Sefa, who reports the anomaly to a Combine liaison out of fear, then regrets it. Emotional beat: guilt; loyalty begins bending toward Bram even as the betrayal is set in motion.

chapters.title: The Inspection That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Combine enforcers board under pretext. Bram hides the ledger shard in the greenhouse's irrigation controller. Emotional beat: cold fear; Bram learns invisibility is a currency already spent.

chapters.title: Course to Dead Space
chapters.summary: Bram lays the plan before the crew: reach the edge relay before the Combine's counter-signal locks the ledger forever. Emotional beat: fragile resolve; three say yes, one lies.

chapters.title: What the Orbits Remember
chapters.summary: Navigator Ilo's POV: charting a route through debris fields from an old corporate war, Ilo recognizes the battle records—her family's ship is in the ledger's casualty lists. Emotional beat: vindication curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Price of Fuel at the End of the World
chapters.summary: A black-market station stop; Bram trades their parent's keepsake for fuel and a warning: the Combine has posted their biometrics. Emotional beat: the cost of inheritance made literal.

chapters.title: Sefa's Confession
chapters.summary: Sefa admits the earlier report. The crew nearly fractures; Bram chooses trust over exile, arguing the ledger is bigger than any betrayal. Emotional beat: forgiveness as a deliberate, costly act.

chapters.title: Gravity Flickers Again
chapters.summary: A second nine-second stutter—closer, deliberate, the failsafe testing its heir. Bram's implants burn with partial keys. Emotional beat: the parent's ghost pressing closer; time is now measurable in stutters.

chapters.title: The Hunter Who Used to Be Crew
chapters.summary: Enforcer Vash Ondrey's POV: a former Kestrel's Wake shipmate now hunting Bram, torn between contract and memory. Emotional beat: the enemy is a mirror of the loyalty theme.

chapters.title: Ambush in the Debris Garden
chapters.summary: Combine drones trap the Kestrel's Wake in the war debris; Ilo threads a suicidal corridor while Bram jettisons their decoy cargo. Emotional beat: terror transformed into fierce, wordless trust.

chapters.title: Half a Key
chapters.summary: The partial key reveals the ledger's final entry: the Combine's plan to scrap the unborn colonists' terraforming contracts entirely. Emotional beat: Bram's garden becomes the stakes; the abstract turns personal.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: First sight of the dead-space relay, derelict and humming with the parent's old infrastructure. Emotional beat: awe and dread—arriving feels like entering a mausoleum built for Bram alone.

chapters.title: Vash's Offer
chapters.summary: Ondrey boards under truce: surrender the key, live rich and anonymous; the Combine will even spare the crew. Emotional beat: temptation articulated perfectly, which is what makes it monstrous.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Weighs
chapters.summary: Crew council. Sefa argues truth; Ilo argues survival; Bram realizes the ledger was designed to force exactly this vote—the parent's last manipulation. Emotional beat: anger transmuted into clarity.

chapters.title: The Counter-Signal Rises
chapters.summary: The Combine's lock-signal reaches the relay's outer band; the window to broadcast begins closing in hours. Emotional beat: ticking-clock dread; no more deliberation, only motion.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Climax part one: a third gravity stutter hits at the relay, and Bram understands the failsafe's final mechanism—the broadcast can only fire during a stutter, and Bram must trigger it manually, inside the field. Emotional beat: terrible comprehension; the inheritance was always a sacrifice.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax: Bram walks the failing relay, holds the key into the stutter, and the ledger pours into every colony's feed while the Kestrel's Wake burns engines to shield the relay from Ondrey's strike team. Emotional beat: transcendence through cost.

chapters.title: After the Signal
chapters.summary: Ondrey, seeing the ledger, stands down and lets them go—choosing memory over contract. The relay dies; the Kestrel's Wake is crippled, adrift. Emotional beat: exhausted, uncertain peace.

chapters.title: Salvage and Silence
chapters.summary: The crew repairs what they can; colonies begin arresting Combine officers on the broadcast's evidence. Bram's name circulates as a ghost story no one can verify. Emotional beat: quiet pride in remaining unseen.

chapters.title: First Planting
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Bram's POV: with the Combine broken, the terraforming contracts hold, and Bram sows the greenhouse's first open cycle—not for the unborn alone, but for people who will know their history. Emotional beat: rootedness; the invisible life, chosen at last.
